themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints surged to 25 THIS WEEK, a 144% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 10.2 weekly complaints, suggesting a potential infrastructure failure or maintenance gap affecting neighborhood safety and visibility.
evidence: 25 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (144% spike, z-score: 5.41)
Statistically significant deviation suggests acute problem rather than normal variation
Safety implications for pedestrians and residents in affected blocks
reporting_angles: Which blocks or intersections are darkened? Map the outages and interview residents about safety concerns.
Has NYCDOT received unusual equipment failures or staffing shortages this week?

themes_detail.label: Curb Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK, a 200% increase from the 8-week average of 3.0 weekly complaints, indicating rapid street-level infrastructure decay that may signal broader pavement or drainage system issues.
evidence: 9 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (200% spike, z-score: 4.9)
Complements broader street condition spike last week (151 complaints, 246% above baseline)
Suggests localized or citywide street maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Is there a geographic cluster of curb damage (specific avenues or cross-streets)?
Interview DOT about maintenance priorities and whether weather or budget constraints are causing delays.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retail Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a staggering 1233% increase from the 8-week average of 0.4 weekly complaints, suggesting rapid illegal storefront openings or community backlash against existing operations on the Upper West Side.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% spike, z-score: 6.65—highest severity spike in dataset)
Represents the most statistically anomalous complaint category in the dataset
Suggests emerging enforcement gap or rapid expansion of underground retail
reporting_angles: Which streets or blocks have illegal cannabis retailers? Conduct walking tour documenting storefronts and signage.
Why is enforcement lagging? Interview NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs about closure timelines and complaint response rates.
Are complaints driven by product quality/safety concerns, odor, or customer behavior?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 151 LAST WEEK, a 246% increase over the 8-week average of 43.6 weekly complaints, representing the largest absolute spike in 311 complaints and suggesting either acute weather damage or systemic maintenance collapse.
evidence: 151 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 43.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (246% spike, z-score: 4.14)
Largest absolute complaint volume in spike dataset; correlates with curb damage surge THIS WEEK
May indicate pothole proliferation, drainage failures, or weather-induced cracking
reporting_angles: Document specific streets with worst conditions (potholes, sinkholes, flooding risk) with photos/video.
Has recent weather (rain, freeze-thaw cycles) triggered accelerated deterioration? Check NYC weather data.
Interview DOT district manager on repair backlog and timeline for street resurfacing in affected corridors.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, a 700% increase from the 8-week average of 0.8 weekly complaints, pointing to disruptive activity in a specific park or new outdoor event patterns as weather improves.
evidence: 6 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.82)
Timing (spring season) suggests seasonal recreation increase, but magnitude unusual
Likely concentrated in one or two parks (Riverside, Central Park area)
reporting_angles: Which park(s) are generating complaints? Riverside Park events, street performers, or late-night gatherings?
Interview Parks Department and local precinct on noise enforcement and new permit approvals for events.
Speak to nearby residents about what specific times/activities are problematic.
